$comment: Generated from comline_core::package::config::keys; regenerate with `COMLINE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p comline-core --lib config::keys`.

keys.description: The edition of the schema language this package is written in, as a number; this core knows edition 1. A change that would break schemas already written ships in a new edition, and a package keeps its behaviour until it moves to it. Every package states one.
keys.summary: The edition of the schema language this package is written in

keys.description: The package's identity for the compatibility check: 32 lowercase hex digits. `comline new` and `comline build` write one when it's missing. A rename keeps it, a copy must change it, and changing it is a major change.
keys.summary: The package's identity, written by comline build

keys.description: Declares what this package can be compiled to. Its only key is `languages`. Per-target output (directory, layout, package versions) lives in `comline.toml`'s `[generate]` table, not here.
keys.summary: What this package can be compiled to

fields.description: The `language#version` targets this package declares it can generate. Each entry's value must be an empty dict (`lang#ver = {}`: it takes no options). A target is checked against the generators the CLI has when the package is generated, not here.
fields.summary: Targets this package can generate, checked by the generators

entry.description: A language and the version of its generator, written `rust#1.70.0`. The value is `{}`: a declared target takes no options.

keys.description: The package's wire defaults, which both ends of a connection must agree on: `wire = { format = "packed@1" framing = "datagram@3" }`. Leaving out either key gives its default, shown there. A protocol's own `@framing` wins over `framing`.
keys.summary: The wire format and framing both ends speak

fields.description: How values are encoded, `"packed@1"` where left out: fixed-width fields and no tags for `packed@1`, UTF-8 JSON for `json@1`, MessagePack for `msgpack@1`, or a namespaced format the package or a dependency declares under `encodings`. JSON-RPC protocols always speak JSON.
fields.summary: How values are encoded

fields.description: How calls are framed, for every protocol with no `@framing` of its own; `"datagram@3"` where left out. The `datagram` framings are Comline's own binary one: `datagram@3` and `datagram@2` are a connection, where either end can call and several protocols share one transport (`datagram@3` addresses a call by its wire number), `datagram@1` is lockstep, one protocol per transport. `jsonrpc@1` is JSON-RPC 2.0. Or a namespaced framing a package declares under `encodings`.
fields.summary: How calls are framed

keys.description: The handshake each protocol of the package runs when it names none in `@handshake`: a name, `handshake = "comline@2"`, or a dictionary when the handshake takes parameters, `handshake = { name = "comline@2" scope = "package" }`. Left out, it is `comline@2`, or `comline@1` in a package whose protocols can't all run `comline@2`. A protocol's own `@handshake` replaces the package's whole. Only `comline@2` takes parameters.
keys.summary: The handshake the package's protocols run

fields.description: Which handshake the package's protocols run. The same as the plain form: `handshake = "comline@2"` is `{ name = "comline@2" }`.
fields.summary: The handshake

fields.description: Whether a protocol's refusal refuses that protocol alone (`protocol`) or the whole connection (`package`). A parameter of `comline@2`, `protocol` where left out. Each end applies it on its own.
fields.summary: Whether a refusal reaches the protocol or the connection

fields.description: When the consumer has functions the provider lacks: `degrade` connects, and calls to them fail locally; `refuse` refuses the protocol. A parameter of `comline@2`, `degrade` where left out. Each end applies it on its own.
fields.summary: What a consumer with more functions gets

fields.description: When two versions are equal but their shapes differ: `refuse` refuses the protocol, `warn` connects and reports a warning, which gives up version honesty. A parameter of `comline@2`, `refuse` where left out. Each end applies it on its own.
fields.summary: What equal versions with different shapes get

fields.description: Who sends what: `offer` is a hello, an answer and a verdict, `symmetric` has each end send a hello and a verdict. A parameter of `comline@2`, `offer` where left out. Both ends must agree on it.
fields.summary: Who sends what in the handshake

keys.description: The encodings each set of protocols (`@connection = admin`) runs on, keyed by the set's name: `connections = { admin = { wire = { framing = "datagram@3" } handshake = { name = "comline@2" } } }`. What a set leaves out is the package's `wire` or `handshake`. A set needs a handshake that compares protocol by protocol and a framing whose protocol numbers don't depend on position, today `comline@2` with `datagram@3`. A set no protocol is in is an error.
keys.summary: The encodings of each named connection set

entry.description: The set's `wire` and `handshake`, each of which replaces the package's.

fields.description: The set's wire format and framing, which a key left out takes from the package's `wire`. Every protocol in the set speaks them.
fields.summary: The set's wire format and framing

fields.description: How values are encoded, `"packed@1"` where left out: fixed-width fields and no tags for `packed@1`, UTF-8 JSON for `json@1`, MessagePack for `msgpack@1`, or a namespaced format the package or a dependency declares under `encodings`. JSON-RPC protocols always speak JSON.
fields.summary: How values are encoded

fields.description: How calls are framed, for every protocol with no `@framing` of its own; `"datagram@3"` where left out. Or a namespaced framing a package declares under `encodings`.
fields.summary: How calls are framed

fields.description: The handshake the set's protocols run, which the package's `handshake` is where left out. A member's own `@handshake` must agree with it in name and wire parameters.

keys.description: Acknowledges, for the whole package, the guarantees its protocols give up through the package's handshake, wire or settings: one reason, `unverified = "the gateway pins schemas by contract"`, or a reason for each guarantee, `unverified = { schema_agreement = "..." }`. A protocol's own `@unverified` wins where both say.
keys.summary: Guarantees the package gives up, with a reason

fields.description: The reason the package gives up `schema_agreement`, for the protocols that take it from the package.
fields.summary: Why the package gives this guarantee up

fields.summary: Why the package gives this guarantee up

fields.description: The reason the package gives up `bounded_size`, for the protocols that take it from the package.

keys.description: Package-wide authoring policy, applying to every schema by default: which annotations and validators are allowed, bounds, and diagnostic levels. Its keys are the settings registry's, which the language server completes and explains inside the block. A dictionary, or a reference to another package's named settings schema.
keys.summary: Authoring policy for every schema in the package

keys.description: Formats, framings and handshakes beyond the official ones, keyed by a namespaced name (`com.acme.x@1`). Each has a profile, a file in the package that states what it establishes, and may suggest how each language implements it.

entry.description: A namespaced name, `com.acme.x@1`, with the kind of encoding and its profile.

fields.summary: format, framing or handshake

fields.description: The path of the encoding's profile (JSON), relative to the package and inside it. Its kind and name must be this entry's. Conformance vectors sit beside it: `profiles/x.json`'s are `profiles/x.vectors.json`.
fields.summary: The profile's path, inside the package

fields.description: Where each language finds a type implementing the encoding, keyed by language.
fields.summary: Suggested implementations, by language

entry.description: A Path dependency (`path`), a Git dependency (`version` + `uri` + `commit`), or a Registry dependency (`version` + `uri`): which fields are present determines the kind.
entry.summary: A Path, Git, or Registry dependency

fields.description: Local filesystem path to a sibling package, which makes this a Path dependency (no declared version; its version is read from the sibling's own last build).

fields.description: Declared version. Required for Git and Registry dependencies (omit for Path dependencies).
fields.summary: Declared version (Git and Registry dependencies)

fields.description: Source URI. Required for Git and Registry dependencies.

fields.description: Pinned commit hash. Its presence makes this a Git dependency (needs `version` and `uri` too).
